territorial_scope.description: Amends the national Penal Code of Argentina, enacted by the Argentine Congress.

evidence.quote: El Senado y Cámara de Diputados de la Nación Argentina reunidos en Congreso, etc. sancionan con fuerza de Ley:

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends Argentina's Penal Code (Ley 26.388, promulgated 24 June 2008) to add criminal offences for computer-related conduct: unauthorized access to restricted systems and data, interception of electronic communications, computer fraud, damage to computer data and systems, and sexual representations of minors; it also defines digital signature and document terms.
summary.long: Ley 26.388 amends the Argentine Penal Code, sanctioned 4 June 2008 and promulgated 24 June 2008. Article 1 adds definitions of document, signature and private instrument that cover digital documents and digital signatures. Article 2 replaces Art. 128 on representations of minors, with prison terms for producing, distributing or possessing such material and for facilitating access to pornography for minors under fourteen. Article 3 renames the chapter on violation of secrets to cover privacy. Article 4 replaces Art. 153 on opening or intercepting electronic communications, with prison of 15 days to 6 months, up to one year if content is published, and double special disqualification for officials who abuse their functions. Article 5 adds Art. 153 bis on knowing unauthorized access to restricted computer systems or data, with 1 month to 1 year where the target is a public body or a public or financial service provider. Article 6 replaces Art. 155 on publication of private correspondence, with fines and an exemption for acts protecting a public interest. Articles 7 and 8 cover officials revealing secrets and offences involving personal data banks. Article 9 adds computer fraud by manipulation of information systems to Art. 173. Article 10 adds damage to data, programs or systems and distribution of damaging programs to Art. 183. Article 11 aggravates damage (Art. 184) where computer systems of public data or of health, communications, energy or transport services are targeted. Article 12 covers interference with communications and Article 13 covers tampering with evidence. Article 14 repeals Arts. 78 bis and 117 bis(1). The text states no separate entry-into-force date.},

relations.note: Amends the Código Penal by substitution, insertion and heading change: Art. 1 (adds paragraphs to Art. 77), Art. 2 (Art. 128), Art. 3 (heading of Chapter III, Title V, Book II), Art. 4 (Art. 153), Art. 5 (inserts Art. 153 bis), Art. 6 (Art. 155), Art. 7 (Art. 157), Art. 8 (Art. 157 bis), Art. 9 (adds inciso 16 to Art. 173), Art. 10 (adds second paragraph to Art. 183), Art. 11 (Art. 184), Art. 12 (Art. 197), Art. 13 (Art. 255).

notes: Text is Ley 26.388 as sanctioned on 4 June 2008 and promulgated de hecho on 24 June 2008, not a consolidated Código Penal. It amends the Código Penal, so the amended articles appear only as their new wording. Art. 14 repeals Art. 78 bis and inciso 1 of Art. 117 bis. Penalties in Arts. 6 and 13 are fixed peso amounts as written in this text. Art. 1 uses the terms firma digital and documento without defining the digital signature; its definition is not given in this text. The text names no implementing decree, competent authority or firm. No internal inconsistency found.

entities.note: The text is a penal code amendment. It names no firm, facility or public body as addressee or designated authority; Art. 15 only orders communication to the Poder Ejecutivo.

obligations.note: The operative articles (Arts. 2, 4-13) define criminal offences and their penalties, which are enforcement content and are excluded from obligations. Arts. 1 and 3 define terms or change a chapter heading, and Art. 14 repeals provisions. Arts. 14 and 15 contain no duty on any regulated actor or public body. No regulatory duties on firms, providers, platforms or government bodies appear in the text.
